column2: I am of no particular nature; I am of the nature of non-action; I am partless, without appearance; I am neither mind nor sense.
I am neither intellect nor conception; I am not the three bodies; I am not of the form of waking or dream, nor of the nature of deep sleep.
I am not of the form of the three afflictions; I do not have the three desires; for the Self of consciousness I have no hearing or reflection that perfects.
I have nothing of the same kind, nothing of a different kind anywhere; nothing within myself; I have the three kinds of difference nowhere.
The form of mind is unreal, the form of intellect is unreal; ego is not established — I am eternal, everlasting, unborn.
Know the three bodies to be unreal; the three times are always unreal; know the three qualities to be unreal; this one is of the nature of truth, pure.
Know all that is heard to be unreal; all Veda is always unreal; know all scripture to be unreal; I am of the nature of true consciousness.
Know the three forms to be unreal; all beings are always unreal; know all principles to be unreal; this is the fullness, Sadashiva.
Know teacher and disciple to be unreal, and the teacher's mantra then unreal; whatever is seen, know it as unreal; do not know me as of that kind.
Know whatever is thought to be unreal; whatever is reasoning is always unreal; whatever is beneficial, know it as unreal; do not know me as of that kind.
Know all breaths to be unreal, all pleasures unreal; know the seen and heard as unreal; the woven and interwoven as made of the unreal.
Know what is to be done and not to be done as unreal; what is lost and gained as made of the unreal; know pain and no-pain as unreal; all and not-all as made of the unreal.
Know full and not-full as unreal; merit and demerit as made of the unreal; know gain and loss as unreal; victory and defeat as made of the unreal.
Know all sound as unreal; all touch is always unreal; know all form as unreal; all taste as made of the unreal.
Know all smell as unreal; all ignorance as made of the unreal; all is always only unreal; the arising of becoming is only unreal.
All qualities are only unreal; I alone am mere being. One should always see the mantra of one's own Self; one should always practice the mantra of one's own Self.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the sin of the seen; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys other mantras.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the faults of the body; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the sin of birth.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the noose of death; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the sorrow of duality.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the notion of difference; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the sorrow of anxiety.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the disease of the intellect; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the bondage of the mind.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys all diseases; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys all grief.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys desire and the rest in a moment; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the power of anger.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys the modifications of the mind; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys intention and the rest.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys crores of faults; this mantra "I am Brahman" destroys every other system.
This mantra "I am Brahman" destroys ignorance of the Self; this mantra "I am Brahman" gives conquest of the world of the Self.
This mantra "I am Brahman" gives happiness beyond argument; this mantra "I am Brahman" gives non-dullness.
This mantra "I am Brahman" crushes the demons of the non-Self; this "I am Brahman" is a thunderbolt that shatters the mountains called non-Self.
This mantra "I am Brahman" removes the demons called non-Self; this mantra "I am Brahman" will free them all.
This mantra "I am Brahman" gives knowledge-bliss; it is the great mantra of seven crores, giving a hundred crores of births.
Abandoning all mantras, one should practice this mantra; one attains liberation at once — there is not even an atom of doubt.

Kumara asked the Supreme Lord: "Tell me the state of the liberated-while-living and the bodiless liberated." The Supreme Shiva said: I am the Self of consciousness, I am the Supreme Self, I am attributeless, I am higher than the highest. He who stays as the Self alone is called liberated while living.
I am beyond the three bodies; I am pure consciousness. He in whom there is inwardly "I am Brahman" is called liberated while living.
I am of the form of a mass of bliss; I am a mass of supreme bliss. He who has no body and the like, who has the certainty "Brahman," who is full of supreme bliss, is called liberated while living.
He in whom there is no "I" of anything, who stays as mere consciousness, whose inner self is mere consciousness, of the single nature of mere consciousness,
whose self is of full form everywhere, who is the Self remaining everywhere, delighting in bliss, unmanifest, wholly full, of the nature of consciousness,

of the form of pure consciousness, free of all attachment, of eternal bliss, serene, free of other thoughts, devoid of any trace of existence — he is called liberated while living. "Mine is not the mind, not the intellect, not the ego, not the senses.

Mine is not the body at any time; not the breath and the rest anywhere; not illusion is mine, not desire, not anger — I am the supreme.
tejobindu:5:9	Mine is not anything this; mine is not any world anywhere; not fault is mine, not mark, not eye, not mind.

Mine is not ear, nose, tongue or hand; not waking, not dream, not even an atom of the cause.
tejobindu:5:11	Mine is not even the Fourth" — he who thus knows is called liberated while living. "All this is nothing of mine; this all is nowhere mine.

Mine is not time, not place, not thing, not thought; not bathing, not twilight prayer, not deity, not place.
tejobindu:5:13	Mine is not pilgrimage, not service, not knowledge, not state; not bondage, not birth, not word, not the sun.

Mine is not merit, not sin, not work, not the auspicious; not 'I am the individual' — the Self is mine; nothing of the three worlds is mine.
tejobindu:5:15	Mine is not liberation, not duality, not the Veda, not the rite; not near, not far, not awakening, not secret.

Mine is not teacher, not disciple, not inferior, not superior; not Brahma, not Vishnu, not Rudra, not the moon.
tejobindu:5:17	Mine is not earth, not water, not wind, not space; not fire, not lineage, not aim, not becoming.

Mine is not the meditator, not the object of meditation, not meditation, not the mantra; not cold, not heat, not thirst, not hunger.
tejobindu:5:19	Mine is not friend, not enemy, not delusion, not victory; not before, not after, not above, not the directions.

Mine is nothing to be said, even slight; nothing to be heard, even an atom; nothing to go to, even slightly; nothing to be meditated on, even an atom.
tejobindu:5:21	Mine is nothing to be enjoyed, even slightly; nothing to be remembered, even an atom; not pleasure, not attachment, not sacrifice, not dissolution.

Mine is not foolishness, not peace, not bondage, not the dear; not joy or great joy; not stout, not thin.
tejobindu:5:23	Mine is not long, not short; not growth, not decay; superimposition or retraction is not mine; not one, not many.

Mine is not blindness, not dullness, not even an atom of cleverness; not flesh, not blood, not fat, not marrow.
tejobindu:5:25	Mine is not marrow, not bone, not skin — the seven constituents; not white, not red, not blue, not separate.

Mine is not heat, not gain; the primary and secondary are nowhere mine; not delusion, not steadiness, not secret, not family.
tejobindu:5:27	Mine is not to be abandoned, not to be taken; not laughable, not policy; not conduct, not weariness, not dryness, not pleasure.

Mine is not knower, not knowledge, not knowable, not self; not for you, not for me; not you and not I.
tejobindu:5:29	Mine is not old age, not childhood, not even an atom of youth. I am Brahman, I am Brahman — thus is the certainty.
I am consciousness, I am consciousness — he who thus holds is called liberated while living. "I am Brahman alone, I am consciousness alone, or I am the supreme" — no doubt.
By himself the swan, by himself established; by himself one should see by oneself; one should dwell in bliss in the kingdom of one's own Self.
He who himself enjoys the bliss of his own Self is called liberated while living; he himself is the one hero in front, he himself is called the lord.
One who has become Brahman, of quiet mind, made of Brahman-bliss, happy, of clear form, a great silent one — he is bodiless and liberated.
The Self of all, of even form, pure Self, I have arisen; free of the one, the one Self, the Self of all, mere own Self.
I am the unborn Self, the immortal Self; I am myself the Self, imperishable; the Self as aim, the playful Self, silent, of the nature of the Self.
The Self of bliss, the dear Self, the Self of liberation, free of bondage; "I am Brahman alone, I am consciousness alone" — even this is not thought.
He who stays as mere consciousness alone is bodiless and liberated.
Abandoning certainty, even the certainty "I am Brahman," with a heart filled with bliss, he is bodiless and liberated.
He stays abandoning the certainty "all exists" or "does not exist"; "I am Brahman" or "I am not" — he is mere being-consciousness-bliss.
He does not touch the Self with anything, anywhere, at any time; silent, remaining silent, silent, truth — nothing.
The Supreme Self, beyond the qualities, the Self of all, the maker of beings' notions: difference of time, difference of things, difference of place, difference of self —
of him there is no difference whatever; nor does anything exist at all. "I," "you," "that," "this," "he" — the Self of time, devoid of time.
The Self of void, of subtle form, the Self of the universe, devoid of the universe; the Self of gods, devoid of gods; the Self of the measurable, free of measure.
Everywhere the Self devoid of dullness, the inner Self of all, the Self devoid of all intentions, always "I am mere consciousness."
I am the Supreme Self alone, the body of knowledge alone, the Self of the nature of mere being; no other fear of the world whatever.
Individual, "Lord," where are these words? "I am" from Veda and scripture — "this is only consciousness," "I am consciousness" —
he who is void even of such certainty is bodiless and liberated. Perfected in mere consciousness, delighting in his own Self, at ease in his seat,
of unlimited form, free of atomic, gross and the like, the Fourth of the Fourth, supreme bliss — he is bodiless and liberated.
The Self devoid of name and form, of the nature of the happiness of supreme awareness, of form beyond the Fourth, free of good and bad,
the Self of yoga, the yoga-yoked Self, free of bondage and liberation, the Self devoid of quality and non-quality, free of place and time and the rest,
the Self devoid of witness and non-witness, something and nothing, none at all; in whom there is no measure of the world, nor even Brahman-form here.
In his own nature self-luminous, in his own nature self-delighting; bliss beyond speech's reach, himself within reach of speech and mind;
he whose state is beyond the beyond is bodiless and liberated. Who is beyond the mind's modification, the illuminator of the mind's modification,
the Self devoid of all modification is bodiless and liberated. At that time "bodiless," free of remembering the body;
if he remembers even slightly, then he is endowed with all; unseen by others in his outer self, a mass of supreme bliss and consciousness;
unseen by others in his outer self, within the reach of all Vedanta; tasting the nectar-savor of Brahman, the elixir of Brahman-nectar-savor;
attached to the nectar-savor of Brahman, himself the nectar-savor of Brahman; immersed in the nectar-savor of Brahman, worshipping Shiva in Brahman-bliss;
satisfied by the nectar-savor of Brahman, an experiencer of Brahman-bliss; Brahman-bliss and Shiva-bliss, radiant with the savor of Brahman-bliss;
the supreme light of Brahman-bliss, continuous in Brahman-bliss; with the sound of the food of Brahman-bliss-savor, a family of Brahman-bliss;
mounted on the savor of Brahman-bliss, a sole mass of Brahman-bliss consciousness; bearing the savor of Brahman-bliss, filled with the savor of Brahman-bliss;
joined with those of Brahman-bliss, established in the Self of Brahman-bliss. All this is of the nature of the Self; nothing is other than the Self.
All is the Self; I am the Self; the Supreme Self, the highest; of the nature of eternal bliss — he is bodiless and liberated.
Of full form, the great Self, the pleased Self, the everlasting Self, of the form of the inner controller of all, the stainless Self, the selfless;
of changeless nature, pure Self, of peaceful form; the Self of peaceful and unpeaceful nature, free of the sense of unity of the Self;
free of the thought "individual self, supreme Self," whose Self is of liberated and unliberated nature, free of liberated and unliberated;
the Self of the nature of bondage and liberation, free of bondage and liberation; the Self of dual and non-dual nature, free of dual and non-dual;
the Self of the nature of all and not-all, free of all and not-all; of the form of joy and great joy, free of joy and the rest;
the Self devoid of all intentions is bodiless and liberated. The partless Self, the stainless Self, the awakened Self, the non-person Self;
the Self devoid of bliss and the rest, the immortal Self, of immortal nature; of the nature of the three times, free of the three times;
the entire Self, the immeasurable Self, the Self of measure, free of measure; the Self of eternally evident nature, the determination of the eternally evident;
of nature devoid of another, self-luminous devoid of another; the Self measured by knowledge and ignorance and the like, free of knowledge and ignorance;
the Self devoid of eternal and non-eternal, free of here and hereafter; the Self empty of the sixfold means beginning with peace, free of the desire for liberation and the like;
the Self devoid of the gross body, free of the subtle body; the Self devoid of cause and the rest, free of the Fourth and the rest;
the Self devoid of the food-sheath, free of the breath-sheath; the Self devoid of the mind-sheath, free of the knowledge-sheath and the rest;
the Self devoid of the bliss-sheath, free of the five sheaths; the Self of non-conceptual nature, free of the conceptual;
the Self devoid of association with the seen, free of association with sound; always the Self empty of samadhi, free of beginning, middle and end;
the Self devoid of the saying "consciousness is Brahman," free of "I am Brahman"; the Self devoid of "That thou art" and the like, without the notion "this Self";
the Self devoid of what Om signifies, free of all that can be said; the Self devoid of the three states, the imperishable Self, of the nature of consciousness;
the Self devoid of the knowable and the like, whatever this is of Self; the Self devoid of appearing and non-appearing — he is bodiless and liberated.
Look at the Self alone; awaken your own Self; by yourself enjoy your own Self; be established in yourself, O six-faced one.
